name: MMI Data Pipeline
excerpt: Import and export any WordPress or WooCommerce data on a schedule. Product imports show every change for review first.
intro: MMI Data Pipeline moves data into and out of WordPress in three steps: fetch it, review it, then import. For products you see exactly what would change, row by row, before anything is written. It also handles orders, customers, coupons, users, comments, posts, pages, custom post types and taxonomies. The same engine exports in CSV, JSON or XML.

features.text: Field mapping, taxonomy mapping and conditions
Scheduled imports and exports with post-run reports
Product Workbench: browse or search the whole catalog, edit in the table, and make bulk changes with undo
Make a change once, or keep applying it on every catalog run (stock, prices, status, categories and more)
Only fill when empty: an import never overwrites a value a product already has
Supplier promotions: sale dates, promotion costs and a check for sales below cost
Duplicate finder: link the same product from different suppliers and choose the main listing
Product content: suggested titles, descriptions and pictures from the maker's own pages, reviewed before they're written
Reference library: help and knowledge-base pages you read in Chrome are kept with their text and dates, ready to search

requirements: WordPress with WooCommerce, PHP 8.0+. Title and description suggestions use your store's AI connection.
suite_line: scheduled imports and exports of any WordPress or WooCommerce data, with review

screenshots.title: Supplier data sources
screenshots.caption: Every feed the store pulls from, in one table.
features: Connect supplier APIs or upload CSV, TSV, JSON and XML files as sources
Each source's type, status, last fetch and record count at a glance
Fetch on demand, preview the raw data or open a source's logs from the toolbar
Switch taxonomy mapping on or off per source

screenshots.title: Import profile: name and sources
screenshots.caption: A five-step wizard sets up each import profile.
features: Steps for name and sources, keys, fields, attributes, and scope and mode
Drag and drop a file to add it as a new source without leaving the wizard
One profile can pull from several sources, each matched on its own primary key
Save & Close at any step; changes save as you go

screenshots.title: Field mapping
screenshots.caption: Map each supplier's fields to WooCommerce fields.
features: A field picker per supplier, so every feed maps in its own shape
Constants, transforms and conditions on any field
Auto-map source fields, or save the mapping as a preset for other profiles
Advanced fields cover sale pricing, dimensions, gallery images and custom fields

screenshots.title: Scope and mode
screenshots.caption: Decide which products a profile may touch, and what it does to them.
features: Limit a profile to products tagged for it, so suppliers never overwrite each other
Create & Update, Create Only, Update Only or Availability Sync
Update Only keeps pricing and stock current without adding new products
Availability Sync reacts only when products drop out of a feed

screenshots.title: Taxonomy mapping
screenshots.caption: Turn supplier categories and brands into your own terms.
features: Map each supplier value to a WooCommerce category or brand once
Sample products beside every value, so you can check a mapping before saving it
Profile variations, alias rules and a filter for unmapped values
Apply all mappings to existing products in one click

screenshots.title: Review & Compare
screenshots.caption: See exactly what an import will do before it runs.
features: Totals for the full feed: how many products will be created, updated or left alone
Filter by change status, stock, images, coupons, price range, order history and any taxonomy
Search the feed by name, SKU or ID
The preview follows the profile's own mode, so skipped products are shown as skipped

screenshots.title: Row-by-row comparison
screenshots.caption: Your store's value beside the supplier's, for every field.
features: Each product matched to its feed row by the supplier's primary key
Current and incoming values side by side, with up-to-date rows marked
Pages of up to 200 rows, sortable by any column
Only real changes go through on the next run

screenshots.title: Import history
screenshots.caption: Every run, with what it did and how long it took.
features: Created, updated, skipped and failed counts for each run
Filter the history by import profile
Partial runs open a report of the failed records and why they failed
Load the full recent history on demand

screenshots.title: Catalog upkeep
screenshots.caption: The steps every catalog run takes, in order.
features: Clean up duplicate stock data and apply main-listing rules
Feed sync marks XChange and SkuPort products out of stock when they leave the feed, and back when they return
Assign categories to products that have none
Runs on a schedule or now; switch each step on or off

screenshots.title: Standing rules
screenshots.caption: Changes that keep applying to every product that matches.
features: Start from any Workbench search and pick a change
A check before saving warns when a rule would undo itself or fight feed sync
Each rule shows what it changed on the last run
Save a search and load it into any other rule

screenshots.title: Duplicate finder
screenshots.caption: The same product from different suppliers, grouped together.
features: Groups found across your XChange, SkuPort and Plugivery feeds, by maker and name, plus older listings of the same product
Each group's members and the cost spread between suppliers
Choose the main listing. The others are marked out of stock, left out of search and point search engines at the main one
New groups to review are counted apart from groups already linked

screenshots.title: Linked listings
screenshots.caption: Groups already linked, and how each was matched.
features: Matches by shared part number are flagged for review
Remove a member, reassign the customer-facing listing, or unlink a group
Sort by brand, product, members or cost spread
